newsitem.title: USA: U.S. West Coast crudes extend losses with WTI.
newsitem.headline: U.S. West Coast crudes extend losses with WTI.

text.p: U.S. West Coast light crude prices extended losses with spot West Texas Intermediate (WTI) crude, while sluggish trade kept deltas unchanged.
An impasse between buyers and sellers kept differentials flat at $2.30 a barrel under December WTI. The last deal done was a late September sale at minus $2.30 a barrel under October WTI.
Outright prices for ANS stood at $21.70/22.00 a barrel late, down 15 cents from early trade and off 60 cents from Monday.
A trader said Tosco would cut runs by 10,000 barrels per day from Tuesday.
Ultramar Corp began unspecified run cuts at its Wilmington, Calif, refinery over the weekend. Cuts came after workers shut a coker and other units, an industry source said earlier.
Wilmington crude held at $18.90/19 a barrel.
Kern River heavy crude also held, ranging $17.40.17.60 a barrel.
